summary: Monongahela NF's first lookout: a wood-framed cabin on Canaan Mountain near Davis, built 1924, abandoned 1943 for Bearden Knob, dismantled 1946. Now a roadside outcrop.

facts.design: wood-framed, live-in cabin with a wraparound porch, built atop a large rock (not a steel tower)
facts.status_note: Cabin dismantled in 1946; the rock outcrop remains beside Canaan Loop Road

access.note: Roadside loop pulloff off Canaan Loop Road, outside Davis, in Monongahela National Forest

visit.trail_note: No formal trail; the rock is right off the road and connects to Fire Trail 2

events.note: Canaan Mountain Lookout built as a wood-framed, live-in cabin on a rock; the first lookout built by Monongahela National Forest
Bearden Knob Tower erected in 1943 to replace the obsolete Canaan Mountain Lookout, about two miles away
No longer needed for fire detection; abandoned after Bearden Knob was built
Registered January 26, 2017 as US 1648, WV 39; nominated by Brian M. Powell

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLOS register calls the site the Canaan Mountain Fire Tower. The Forest Service report and Mon Forest Towns both describe a wood-framed cabin, not a steel tower. The story follows the Forest Service account.
FFLOS 2008 photo captions show footings. The 2026 Mon Forest Towns guide says only the outcrop remains. The sources do not date the footings' present state, so both are reported.

notes_for_editor: Brief's record (kind ground, gone, built 1924, removed 1946) checks out; access was unknown and is now public per Mon Forest Towns. The FFLOS page calls it a tower; the Forest Service report says cabin, and the story follows the report. The 2008 footings photos and the 2026 outcrop-only description differ. No new photos added: FFLOS images have no verified image URLs here. The Mon Forest Towns guide's rules on removing artifacts from federal land are general, not site-specific.
